subject: Capacity readiness and concurrency tradeoffs — discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@streamlytics.ai>, Adam Chen <adam.chen@streamlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity readiness and concurrency tradeoffs — discovery follow-up

Hi Elena / Adam —

Thanks again for the call this afternoon. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're aligned: we appreciate you walking us through the live usage profile — that context will help shape a focused trial.

Key pain points you called out
- End-user streaming UX drops to chunked/slow responses at peak (bad for live transcription and chat).
- p95 token latency spikes to ~1.2s for 512-token responses during bursts.
- Platform needs predictable cost+latency under concurrency bursts (you see 800–1,200 concurrent streaming sessions during mornings).

Current stack notes you mentioned
- In-house TF/Triton serving with custom batching and a Redis KV cache for prefixes.
- Models: Llama-2-13B quantized (INT8) for most workloads; some experiments with 70B off-hours.
- Observability: limited distributed traces (sampler only), no per-token timing breakdowns.

Success criteria you shared (restated)
- p95 end-to-end token generation latency <= 300ms for typical 256–512 token responses, sustained at 600–800 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming token-by-token smoothness (no visible stalls > 200ms).
- No regression in response quality compared to your current Llama-2 int8 baseline.

Proposed technical trial (high level)
1) 2-week sandbox on Redwood Dedicated (isolated pool) with streaming enabled + prefix/KV cache.
2) Baseline run: replay a 1-hour peak trace you provide (we'll use your sample trace) to reproduce p95 and stalls.
3) Tuning pass: try batching knobs, KV cache warm-up, and small quantization variant (if available) to target p95 <= 300ms.
4) Success verification: run an A/B of your current infra vs Redwood on identical trace + automated quality checks.

Immediate asks from Streamlytics
- Share a 30–60 minute representative trace (relay format ok) and a small masked sample dataset for quality checks.
- Confirm whether the 70B experiments must remain off the trial path (resource constraints).
- Preferred trial window next two weeks (we have slots starting Apr 6).

Attachments: redwood_trial_scope.pdf (trial scope & resource request), sample-trace-format.md (format spec).

Next steps from our side
- I'll propose two calendar slots for a technical kickoff (60m) where we bring one runtime engineer.
- Marissa will follow up on commercial terms for a 2-week Dedicated sandbox.

If that summary looks right, reply with the trace and preferred kickoff window. I can also put together a short checklist to help your infra team prepare (ports, test tokens, sample workload generator).

Best,
Connor O'Brien | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@streamlytics.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Chen <adam.chen@streamlytics.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity readiness and concurrency tradeoffs — discovery follow-up

Thanks, Connor — this covers the call well. A few clarifications and preferences from our side:

Clarifications
- The 1.2s p95 is end-to-end (client -> infer -> client) for 512 tokens. The model generation itself is ~700ms at peak, the remainder is queuing + network interop.
- Bursts: our mornings (08:00–10:00 PT) are the worst; sustained concurrency around 800 with short bursts to ~1,200 for 3–7 minutes.
- We do need to keep the 70B experiments off the trial; the team is OK with focusing on 13B quantized variants for now.

Data sharing:
- I'll upload a masked sample trace (includes timing stamps + payload sizes) to the Drive link you listed by EOD. Filename: sample-trace-20270331.json.
- We can provide a 10k-message replay script (Adam will attach).

Risk/constraints to flag
- Security: any sandbox must be isolated (no cross-tenant logging) and must support our KMS for key rotation.
- Observability: we need per-token/stream timestamps to validate streaming smoothness; if Redwood can emit per-token timing via tracing, that would be ideal.

Preferred kickoff: Apr 7 or Apr 8 (anytime after 10:00 PT).

Thanks — looking forward.

Elena
Elena Morales | Head of Platform
Streamlytics
elena.morales@streamlytics.ai | +1 (617) 222-4433

- I'll confirm when we see the upload and coordinate with our runtime team to do an initial dry replay the same day you upload.

2) Observability
- We can emit per-token timing via a short tracing wrapper in the trial; I will coordinate runtime instrumentation with our engineer (requesting 1 runtime engineer for the kickoff).

3) Security/KMS
- For the sandbox we'll provision an isolated Dedicated pool and accept your KMS integration; Marissa, can you own the security checklist and provide the template for their InfoSec review?

4) Kickoff slot
- I'll reserve Apr 7 at 10:30 PT as the first option and Apr 8 at 11:00 PT as backup — please confirm which works.

If agreeable, we'll spin up the trial environment the morning after kickoff and run the replay during the first 24 hours to capture a baseline.

Connor

Subject: INTERNAL: Streamlytics trial prep & resource ask (summary)

Internal note — quick summary and ask after Elena confirmed upload window. This message is internal only.

Summary of external asks
- Receive sample-trace-20270331.json and replay script from Streamlytics (Elena/Adam).
- KMS integration for sandbox (InfoSec signoff required).
- Kickoff: Apr 7 10:30 PT (tentative).

Internal action items
- Connor: coordinate runtime engineer for Apr 7 kickoff (assigning Miguel from runtime team; need his confirmation).
- Marissa: prepare security checklist and draft sandbox SOW + pricing for 2-week Dedicated sandbox (include expected GPU hours and uplift).
- Lauren: approve expedited quota increase for Dedicated pool (short term; 2 weeks).

Notes for the trial plan (technical)
- Baseline replay within first 24 hours of environment availability; capture per-token timings and collector traces.
- Focus tuning on batching policy + prefix KV warm-up; if needed test small model variant (13B int8 vs 13B int8 + small quantization tweak) but avoid 70B.
- Success metric: p95 <= 300ms sustained at 800 concurrent streaming sessions (target stretch to 600–1,000 to capture burst envelope).

Attachments for internal folder: redwood_trial_scope.pdf, runtime-checklist.md (I put them in the synced trial folder).

Please confirm owners and I'll convert this into a quick playbook for the kickoff.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
